title: deployment.rollback is wired in the daemon, fenced human-only and MCP-excluded, refusing fail-closed
description:
SPIDR prerequisite of task-95e68a8dd2464e7b8ad4b1f8c4d2b2e4, cut by architect-b63fabf3 on 2026-09-05. dependsOn the contract row task-37a50989 because `ROWS.kind` in the daemon roster tests is typed `RuntimeCommandKind` - this row cannot even TYPECHECK before that lands.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: the daemon half of `deployment.rollback` - the family table, the WiredCommandKind union, PAYLOAD_KEYS, OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS, a registry entry refusing FAIL-CLOSED until the effect lands, the three hand-written roster tests and their count pins, plus the operator fence: MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS and HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS with their own count pins.

ROLLING BACK A PRODUCTION ENVIRONMENT IS NEVER AN AGENT'S DECISION. That is why the fence is in this row rather than deferred: the kind must be unreachable over MCP from the moment the registry serves it, not from the moment the effect works. The MCP port authenticates with the operator bootstrap credential, so an MCP caller would arrive AS the operator - exclusion is the fence, and a capability gate is not.

TWO MEASURED FACTS TO SAVE A REDISCOVERY:
- The bidirectional set-equality DoD-4 of the parent asked for ALREADY EXISTS at daemon-command-registry.test.ts - it compares `[...deps.registry.keys()].sort()` (the dispatch seam) against ROWS with BOTH directions spelled out. Do NOT write a parallel arm; move its count pins and let the existing assertion do its job. Same for the per-transport MCP unreachability sweeps in mcp-main.test.ts and mcp-http-host.test.ts, which `.map` over MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS and generate their cases automatically.
- HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS is ONE Set at orchestrator/agent-spawn-contract.ts, re-exported by agent-wrapper.ts. Several task descriptions on this board still claim it is duplicated byte-for-byte; that is STALE. Verify before planning against it.

COUNT PINS ARE THE ACTUAL WORK. Publishing a kind moves ~10 literals across four test files, including a DERIVED one (`EXCLUSION_CASES.length * MCP_TRANSPORT_ENTRY_COUNT`) that reads as an unrelated fact and is the likeliest omission. `git grep -n 'toBe(N)|toHaveLength(N)'` before and after; take every number from the PRINTED expected-vs-received, never from arithmetic, because sibling kind-publishing rows move the same literals.

NOT IN SCOPE: the rollback EFFECT (redeploying the previous image, the DB restore, the health probe) - its successor row. The backups - task-95e68a8d. The contract roster - task-37a50989.

VERIFY: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`.
definitionOfDone: `deployment.rollback` is wired across the daemon roster: the family table, the WiredCommandKind union, PAYLOAD_KEYS (whose key ORDER is the served order), OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS, and a registry entry. `agentCapabilitiesFor` returns null for it - never staffable, whatever its family capability says.

IT IS OPERATOR-ONLY AND MCP-EXCLUDED: the kind is in MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS and in HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS, and a test asserts an agent-authenticated dispatch is refused while an operator-authenticated one reaches the handler - asserting the specific reason CODE and the LAYER that refused, never merely that it failed.

The registry entry REFUSES FAIL-CLOSED until the effect lands: a well-formed payload gets a stable refusal code with its layer read from a closed code->layer map, never a literal. Say in the completion record that this is a deliberate stub and name the successor row that replaces it - do not write a test arm whose only purpose is to reach the stub.

EVERY COUNT PIN MOVED, enumerated by file:line in the completion record. Run `git grep -n 'toBe(<old>)|toHaveLength(<old>)' -- apps/daemon/src` before and after and show the after-count is zero. The derived arithmetic pin in mcp-main.test.ts moves too - it is the likeliest omission because its literal is not the number being changed.

The EXISTING bidirectional set-equality assertion (daemon-command-registry.test.ts, registry.keys() vs ROWS) and the existing per-transport MCP sweeps stay green with their pins moved, and NO parallel arm is added - they already generate this kind's cases. Prove both directions with a mutation drill: delete the PAYLOAD_KEYS entry and delete the ROWS entry, each on its own, and quote both reds.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` is NOT evidence for this row - vitest.config.ts has no apps/** in its include.
taskRails: ROLLBACK IS HUMAN-ONLY. Operator-principal, MCP-excluded, in HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS, and never staffable. Rolling back a production environment is not an agent's decision, and the fence lands with the registry entry rather than after it.

REFUSE FAIL-CLOSED until the effect lands. A well-formed payload gets a stable code with its layer from a closed map - never a literal, never a fifth invented code, and never a test arm whose only job is to reach the stub.

DO NOT WRITE A PARALLEL ROSTER TEST. The bidirectional set-equality and the per-transport MCP sweeps already exist and auto-generate this kind's cases. Move their count pins; adding an arm is duplicate coverage.
NO COUNT LITERAL IS TRUSTWORTHY. Sibling rows publish kinds concurrently. Take every number from the PRINTED expected-vs-received at the moment of the final gate.
NO EFFECT, NO BACKUPS, NO UI, NO CONTRACT ROSTER: each belongs to a named sibling.

implementationPlan.description: MEASURE THE PINS YOURSELF — EVERY NUMBER IN THIS PLAN IS ALREADY STALE BY DESIGN. NO EDITS. (a) THIS ROW WAS NARROWED AFTER A HARD REJECT. Its first plan came in at 12 files and was refused (`[CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION] Plan too large: 12 distinct affected files (max 10)`), so the OPERATOR FENCE moved to task-2ab7b462 — MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS, HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS and the six files carrying their count pins are NOT yours. This row is the DAEMON ROSTER only. DoD-2 of the text you are reading belongs to that row; where description and plan disagree, THE PLAN IS AUTHORITY. Note the consequence and do not try to fix it here: between this row and that one the kind is SERVED and MCP-ADVERTISED, refusing fail-closed — an advertised tool that declines, not a reachable rollback. That row is CRITICAL and depends only on this one. (b) CONFIRM THE PREREQUISITE: `grep -n 'deployment.rollback' packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts` must hit — `ROWS.kind` is typed `RuntimeCommandKind`, so this row cannot TYPECHECK before task-37a50989 lands. If absent, moe.report_blocked with blockedOnTaskIds ['task-37a50989105c40de9fe069d739df9595'] and stop. (c) A SIBLING IS MOVING THE SAME LITERALS RIGHT NOW: `deployment.deploy` and `deployment.set_target` are on the CONTRACT roster but NOT in the daemon vocabulary (`grep -c 'deployment.deploy' apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.ts` = 0 at plan time), so task-04b3ce7e's daemon half is still to come and moves every count below. TAKE EVERY NUMBER FROM THE PRINTED EXPECTED-VS-RECEIVED of a failing run, never from this plan and never from arithmetic. (d) THE CENSUS, AS A MAP OF LOCATIONS: DAEMON ROSTER 47 — `daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts:254` (ROWS) and `:255` (distinct-kind set); `daemon-command-registry.test.ts:862` (ROWS), `:863` (registry.size), `:870` (REGISTRATION_ORDER), and THREE MORE ~850 lines further down at `:1722` ports.registry.size, `:1744` supplied.registry.size, `:1776` snapshotPorts.registry.size — those three are the classic omission, so grep rather than eyeball. OPERATOR_ONLY 12 — `vocabulary.test.ts:346` and `:347` (OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS.size), `registry.test.ts:1040` and `:1041`. Run `git grep -n 'toBe(47)|toHaveLength(47)|toBe(12)|toHaveLength(12)' -- apps/daemon/src` before starting and again at the end, and beware false positives — unrelated suites pin the same numbers; only the files named above are yours. (e) BASELINE, standalone foreground, quoting each count line: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. (f) `git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src` and note peer dirt.

WIRE THE VOCABULARY. `daemon-command-vocabulary.ts` and `daemon-command-families.ts`. (1) Import the kind and add `typeof` it to the WiredCommandKind union. (2) GIVE IT A FAMILY TABLE ENTRY and put that table in FAMILY_TABLES — this is load-bearing, not decoration: `familyCapabilityOf` returns null for an unclaimed kind and `requiredCapabilityOf` THROWS on that null while BUILDING the registry, so a missing entry fails at daemon boot rather than in a test. (3) Add it to OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS with a one-line why-comment in the neighbours' voice. (4) Make `agentCapabilitiesFor` return null for it — never staffable, whatever its family capability says; `product_contract.answer_clarification` is the shape to copy, and put it beside that line rather than at the end of the function. (5) Add its PAYLOAD_KEYS entry. PAYLOAD_KEYS KEY ORDER IS THE SERVED ORDER — the registry maps `Object.keys(PAYLOAD_KEYS)` through `entryOf` — so the position you choose here is the position you must transcribe into REGISTRATION_ORDER in step 4, which is transcribed in INSERTION order and not alphabetically. (6) `daemon-command-families.ts`: add the membership predicate and return the kind's capability BEFORE the `familyCapabilityOf` fallthrough. Do NOT set a flag that routes the kind into an existing service's dispatch branch — that is how a new kind silently inherits another family's handler.

SERVE IT, FAIL-CLOSED. `daemon-command-registry.ts`. The entry REFUSES until task-da60dc4b lands the effect, and the refusal must be honest rather than a placeholder. Decode the payload with an exact-key decoder and refuse on a malformed one; refuse a WELL-FORMED one with a stable code whose LAYER COMES FROM A CLOSED code->layer MAP, never a literal at the throw site. That closed map is the whole point: it makes it structurally impossible for a call site to mint a code and a layer that disagree, which is the defect the pattern exists to prevent. Reuse an already-rostered layer literal — introduce no new `*_LAYER` constant, which would demand a boundary-roster backfill this row does not own. Place the branch where the kind's shape actually belongs: it has no codec, so reaching the generic `requestOf` assembly would throw the wrong error entirely — put it with the kinds whose request shape is exact and disjoint, before that call. Keep the addition to a handful of lines and reformat nothing: this file was already over the 400-line cap at merge-base, which is a pre-existing condition this diff must not worsen. SAY IN THE COMPLETION RECORD that the stub is deliberate and name task-da60dc4b as its replacement — and do NOT write a test arm whose only purpose is to reach it.

MOVE THE ROSTER PINS — AND WRITE NO PARALLEL SET-EQUALITY TEST. Read this before adding an assertion: THE BIDIRECTIONAL SET-EQUALITY ALREADY EXISTS. `daemon-command-registry.test.ts` compares `[...deps.registry.keys()].sort()` — the DISPATCH SEAM, which is what global rail 9 asks for — against `ROWS.map(kind).sort()`, with both directions spelled out. Adding your ROWS entry and your PAYLOAD_KEYS entry makes that existing arm cover this kind automatically. Writing a second one is duplicate coverage and a reject. THE EDITS: (1) `daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts` — a ROWS entry (agent null, its capability, its family, its payloadKeys), the two 47s at :254-255, the OPERATOR_ONLY roster and both 12s at :346-347. (2) `daemon-command-registry.test.ts` — the matching ROWS entry carrying the fail-closed stub's refusal CODE and LAYER, the kind transcribed into REGISTRATION_ORDER at THE SAME INDEX it occupies in PAYLOAD_KEYS, the OPERATOR_ONLY roster and both 12s at :1040-1041, and SIX 47s: :862, :863, :870, :1722, :1744, :1776. (3) `daemon-store-dependencies.test.ts` — insert the kind into the hand-written `registryKinds` SET in SORTED order; that file's own comment says a new command writes its own kind there, and it is a separate roster from the two above.

DRILLS, GATES, SELF-REVIEW. (a) DRILLS. `git status --porcelain` the exact mutated paths FIRST. EVERY FILE IN THIS ROW IS TRACKED and it creates none, so an empty `git diff -- <path>` is the correct restore proof for each, in a call SEPARATE from the restore — state that explicitly and note that global rail 13's untracked/SHA256 clause does NOT apply here, rather than performing a ritual that proves nothing on a tracked path. THREE DRILLS: (i) and (ii) BOTH DIRECTIONS OF THE SET-EQUALITY, which is the row's central property and needs two drills because one direction proves half of it — delete the PAYLOAD_KEYS entry only and confirm the existing arm reds in the SERVED-BUT-UNADVERTISED direction, quoting the set DIFFERENCE rather than a bare count; then restore, delete the ROWS entry only, and confirm it reds the other way. (iii) Remove the family table entry only and confirm the failure is a registry BUILD error rather than a quiet capability default — that is what proves the entry is load-bearing and not decoration. (b) GATES — standalone foreground, one command per call, no pipes and no `;` chains, quoting each `Test Files N passed` count line: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` is NOT evidence — vitest.config.ts has no `apps/**`. Re-run the step-1 census grep and show ZERO stale literals remain in YOUR files. Attribute red by failing paths at HEAD minus the step-1 baseline, intersected with this row's owned paths — and note that task-04b3ce7e's daemon half may land mid-flight and move the same numbers; a red naming a count you did not touch is likely theirs. (c) ADVERSARIAL PASS on this diff only: is the kind spelled IDENTICALLY in the production roster and in every hand-written transcription (a typo reds as a set difference, not a helpful message); does REGISTRATION_ORDER's index match PAYLOAD_KEYS' insertion position; did the family predicate accidentally route the kind into an existing service's dispatch branch instead of your stub; does the stub's layer come from the closed map rather than a literal (grep your own diff for a bare layer string); did you touch mcp-tool-allowlist.ts, agent-spawn-contract.ts or packages/contracts — all of which belong to other rows. (d) COMPLETION RECORD must state: every pin moved by file:line with before/after grep counts; that the bidirectional set-equality was REUSED rather than duplicated, naming the arm so a QA reading DoD-5 does not hunt for a new test; that the registry entry is a DELIBERATE fail-closed stub replaced by task-da60dc4b; that the operator fence is task-2ab7b462's and the kind is MCP-ADVERTISED until it lands, refusing fail-closed in the meantime; and that no `*_LAYER` constant was introduced.

comments.content:
NARROWED AFTER A HARD REJECT — THE FENCE MOVED OUT. architect-b63fabf3, 2026-09-05, HEAD f3b94eaa. Plan approved: 5 steps, 6 files. Where description and plan disagree, THE PLAN IS AUTHORITY.

I filed this row this afternoon and its first plan came in at **12 files** and was refused (`max 10`). The operator fence — `MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS`, `HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS` and the six files carrying their count pins — is now **task-2ab7b462** (CRITICAL, `dependsOn` this row). DoD-2 of the description belongs there.

## The seam is forced, not chosen

Two constraints pull against each other:

1. `mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts` asserts every excluded kind is a real `PAYLOAD_KEYS` key **and still served** — so the exclusion cannot land *before* the wiring.
2. Four test files pin `MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS.length` and two more pin a **derived product** of it — so the roster and its pins must land in **one** commit or the branch is red in between.

Wiring-then-fence is the only order where every commit is green. Putting the roster here and its pins next would leave a knowingly-red branch.

## The interim, stated precisely rather than alarmingly

Between the two rows the kind is **served and MCP-advertised**. But this row's registry entry refuses **fail-closed**, so an MCP caller finds an advertised tool that declines — *"advertised but refusing"*, not *"an agent can roll back production"*.

That is exactly why the stub's refusal must be real: a stub throwing an uncoded error, or one whose layer came from a literal instead of the closed map, would turn a bounded hole into an unclear one.

## The pin census is a map of LOCATIONS, not values

**My own memo from this morning is already wrong.** It recorded the exclusion roster at 6 and its derived pin at 12; measured today they are **11 and 22**. The daemon roster moved **46 → 47** and OPERATOR_ONLY **11 → 12** within the same day, and `deployment.deploy`'s daemon half is *still unlanded* (`grep -c` in the vocabulary = 0) and will move them again.

So the plan gives file:line and forbids taking the values. Three specifics:

- **Three distant 47s** at registry.test.ts `:1722`, `:1744`, `:1776` — ~850 lines below their siblings. Grep, don't eyeball.
- **A third hand-written roster** in `daemon-store-dependencies.test.ts`, separate from the two obvious ones.
- **The census grep has false positives** — unrelated suites pin the same numbers. Editing one because the grep matched is a foreign change that will look deliberate.

## Two things not to do

**Don't write a parallel set-equality test.** It already exists against the dispatch seam (`registry.keys()` vs `ROWS`, both directions) and covers this kind automatically once the two rosters gain it.

**Don't add the family table entry late.** `familyCapabilityOf` returns null for an unclaimed kind and `requiredCapabilityOf` throws on it *while building the registry* — i.e. at daemon boot, not in a test. Drill (iii) proves that entry is load-bearing rather than decoration.
